template.why: A template is a document the user already copied into their own workspace; the lockfile entry is flagged and the template can no longer be used from the marketplace, but copies already made are the user's own files and are not recalled.

skill.mechanism: Reconcile flags the lockfile entry first, then adapter.revoke() removes the skill from Hermes (a missing skill counts as removed); retried each reconcile until it succeeds.

routine.mechanism: Ledger marked revoked first (the scheduler filter skips it on the next tick), then the managed cron job is removed via hermes marketplace revoke.

memory.mechanism: hermes marketplace revoke marks the ledger, then reverts the memory provider to the one recorded in memory-binding.json; stored memory data is left untouched.

hook.mechanism: Ledger revoked flag read by the hook engine on every event (inert in the running process), then the applied declarative hook entries are removed.

bridge.mechanism: Ledger flag first (the guard blocks the next call in the running gateway), then the mcp_servers entry and the grant are removed.

connector.mechanism: Ledger flag first (guard blocks calls), then the mcp_servers entry, the managed .env block, grants and instances are removed; the keychain secret is deleted.

workflow.mechanism: Ledger flag first (the next run is refused), then the applied definition is removed; an in-flight tool call finishes.

agent.mechanism: The agent profile becomes an inert tombstone (managed files and skills leave, profile data stays) via adapter.revoke().

bundle.why: A bundle is only a record; its members are real installs of other types and each is revoked through its own adapter (dependency_revoked), so there is nothing applied to the bundle itself.

surface.why: Surface is unsupported and never installed, so nothing is ever applied that could need revoking; the not-available adapter revoke is a no-op.
